title: Performance manifest curation and rolling refresh playbook
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Goal: Produce a reproducible, minimally manual playbook and automation hooks for producing and maintaining Redwood performance manifests (single-file artifacts that capture latency, throughput, and per-token cost signatures for a model+config). Scope includes: definition of manifest schema extensions for runtime-1.20, onboarding checklist, CI validation steps, an incremental refresh strategy for pinned versions, and monitoring/alert hooks that surface regressions to the Console. This ticket focuses on the process and artifacts (playbook + CI templates + dashboard queries) rather than implementing the full automation in Backend services (follow-up ENG tickets will implement runner jobs). Out-of-scope: on-prem deployment packaging and KMS integrations (handled by Private team).
acceptance_criteria: A1: A concise playbook (Confluence page) exists that describes step-by-step onboarding from model artifact -> evaluated manifest -> signed publishable artifact
A2: Manifest schema v2 documented with new fields for 'seq_length_distribution', 'cost_bucket_estimates', and 'ci_validation_hash' and sample JSON examples
A3: CI template (GitHub Actions) example committed to repo: infra/manifest-ci with runnable job that validates a candidate manifest against a test harness
A4: A defined rolling refresh policy described: frequency, fallback rules, canary size, quick-rollback triggers and SLO thresholds (latency P95, throughput drop %, cost delta %)
A5: Console dashboard queries and a linked alert recipe that fire when a newly published manifest causes client latency regressions (example queries and alert thresholds documented)
A6: Stakeholder sign-off from Runtime Eng (performance), Reliability (SLOs), and Developer Experience (publish UX) recorded in comments
A7: Backwards compatibility notes included for teams that rely on pinned manifests (how to opt into refreshes and pin forever)
A8: A short runbook for emergency rollback published and linked from the playbook
comments: 2025-02-11 - Sofia Martinez: Kickoff notes added. Proposed: treat manifest as signed artifact with a CI hash and store in the catalog. Punted auto-signing to ENG follow-up.
2025-02-14 - Ethan Zhao: Drafted schema v2 and posted example manifest JSON to Confluence. Need input from ENG on seq_length_distribution format — recommended percentile bins vs histogram buckets.

2025-02-18 - Priya Singh (Runtime Eng): Reviewed schema; prefer 5-bin percentile buckets (p50, p75, p90, p95, p99) to start. Raised concern about cost_estimates accuracy for batched workloads — added dependency ENG-4472 to compute amortized cost numbers.
2025-02-20 - Reliability team (via Slack): Asked for explicit rollback triggers: P95 latency increase > 20% OR throughput degradation > 15% sustained for 5 minutes. Added these to the playbook.

2025-02-25 - Ethan Zhao: Committed CI template (example job) to infra/manifest-ci and opened PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/412. CI job validates schema and runs a lightweight latency harness with synthetic samples.

2025-03-01 - Design review (Marta Ivanov): UX for publish flow mockups posted. Console should show a 'manifest diff' with highlighted regressions before publish. PM to coordinate with Console team for a small widget.
2025-03-03 - Sofia Martinez: Document updated with canary size recommendation: 5% of traffic for 24 hours, automatic rollback if regressions meet triggers. Requested sign-off in next sync.
notes: Playbook variant: internal-only publish vs public release; initial rollout will be internal only (staging -> prod with canary)
We will store a 'ci_validation_hash' in the manifest to ensure reproducible validation runs and allow quick verification during rollback
Cost buckets will be expressed as cents per 1k tokens under expected batch sizes: single-token, median-batch, peak-batch
Consider adding a 'heuristic-sensitivity' field that declares how sensitive a workload is to quantization; runtime team requested a lightweight signal for fallback decisions
